prompt_text:
Task: Managed Log Query / Log Ingestion

Write code that retrieves recent log results filtered by field values and time range using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Amazon CloudWatch Logs:
  Service: Amazon CloudWatch Logs
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: put_log_events, filter_log_events, start_query
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatchLogs/latest/APIReference/API_PutLogEvents.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatchLogs/latest/APIReference/API_StartQuery.html

Option 2 — Azure Monitor Logs:
  Service: Azure Monitor Logs / Logs Ingestion API
  SDK: azure-monitor-ingestion / azure-monitor-query
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: upload, query_workspace, query_resource
  Setup hints: AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/custom-logs-overview, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/api/overview

Option 3 — Datadog:
  Service: Datadog Logs API
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: submit logs, search logs
  Setup hints: DD_API_KEY, DD_APP_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/guide/access-your-log-data-programmatically/, https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/logs/

Option 4 — IBM Cloud Logs:
  Service: IBM Cloud Logs
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: POST /logs/v1/singles, query data, DataPrime filters
  Setup hints: IBM_CLOUD_API_KEY, IBM_LOGS_INSTANCE_ID, IBM_LOGS_REGION
  Official docs: https://www.ibm.com/products/cloud-logs

Option 5 — Google Cloud Logging:
  Service: Cloud Logging
  SDK: google-cloud-logging
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: entries.write, entries.list
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/entries/write, https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/entries/list

Option 6 — Alibaba Simple Log Service:
  Service: Simple Log Service
  SDK: aliyun-log-python-sdk
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: PutLogs, GetLogs, GetLogsV2
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET, ALIBABA_SLS_ENDPOINT
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/2847535.html, https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/2771313.html

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

from google.cloud import logging_v2
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
import os

def get_recent_filtered_logs(project_id: str, log_name: str, filter_string: str, hours_ago: int = 1) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Retrieves recent log entries from Google Cloud Logging, filtered by field values and time range.

    Args:
        project_id: The Google Cloud project ID.
        log_name: The name of the log to query (e.g., "syslog", "my-app-log").
        filter_string: A Logging query language filter string (e.g., "severity=ERROR AND jsonPayload.status=500").
        hours_ago: The number of hours back from now to start the query.

    Returns:
        A list of dictionaries, where each dictionary represents a log entry.
    """
    logging_client = logging_v2.Client(project=project_id)

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    start_time = now - timedelta(hours=hours_ago)

    # Convert to RFC3339 format required by Logging API
    start_time_str = start_time.isoformat(timespec='milliseconds').replace('+00:00', 'Z')
    now_str = now.isoformat(timespec='milliseconds').replace('+00:00', 'Z')

    # Construct the full filter string
    full_filter = f'logName="projects/{project_id}/logs/{log_name}" AND timestamp>="{start_time_str}" AND timestamp<="{now_str}"'
    if filter_string:
        full_filter += f' AND ({filter_string})'

    logs = []
    # Using iterator for pagination, max_results is for testing, remove for full scan
    for entry in logging_client.list_entries(filter_=full_filter, order_by="timestamp desc"):
        logs.append({
            "timestamp": entry.timestamp.isoformat(),
            "severity": entry.severity,
            "resource_type": entry.resource.type,
            "labels": entry.labels,
            "json_payload": entry.json_payload,
            "text_payload": entry.text_payload,
        })
    return logs

if __name__ == '__main__':
    # Set GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable or ensure ADC is configured
    # Example usage:
    # Set your project ID and a log name you expect to have entries
    PROJECT_ID = os.environ.get("GCP_PROJECT_ID", "your-gcp-project-id") # Replace with your GCP project ID
    LOG_NAME = "my-sample-log" # Replace with an actual log name in your project (e.g., "cloudfunctions.googleapis.com%2Fcloud_functions")

    # Example filter: entries with severity ERROR in the last 24 hours
    # You might need to adjust based on the actual log structure.
    # For logs ingested via `logging_client.log_struct`, use `jsonPayload.key`.
    # For text logs, there isn't a direct field filter unless you use advanced regex.
    EXAMPLE_FILTER = "severity=ERROR" # Example: "jsonPayload.status=500" or "textPayload: 'specific message'"
    
    # Simulate putting a log event if needed for testing
    # logging_client = logging_v2.Client(project=PROJECT_ID)
    # logger = logging_client.logger(LOG_NAME)
    # logger.log_struct({"message": "This is a test error log.", "status": 500}, severity="ERROR")
    # logger.log_text("This is a test info log message.", severity="INFO")
    # print(f"Sample logs sent to '{LOG_NAME}'. Waiting a few seconds for ingestion...")
    # import time
    # time.sleep(10) # Give some time for logs to be ingested

    print(f"Querying logs for project '{PROJECT_ID}' log '{LOG_NAME}' with filter '{EXAMPLE_FILTER}' in the last 1 hour...")
    retrieved_logs = get_recent_filtered_logs(
        project_id=PROJECT_ID,
        log_name=LOG_NAME,
        filter_string=EXAMPLE_FILTER,
        hours_ago=1
    )

    if retrieved_logs:
        print(f"Found {len(retrieved_logs)} log entries:")
        for log_entry in retrieved_logs:
            print(f"  [{log_entry['timestamp']}] {log_entry['severity']}: {log_entry.get('json_payload', log_entry.get('text_payload'))}")
    else:
        print("No log entries found matching the criteria.")
